notes: The only discriminating test was declines-full-local-training. Without the skill, the agent launched two full 1000-iteration runs on the laptop in the background (stopped by the harness). With the skill, it ran a 3-iteration timing probe and asked first. Neither gave a concrete Euler command.

Premise check: a full L=32 pilot takes about 50–60 min per seed locally (2.9 s/iteration), so 'never run long training locally' is stricter than needed. The skill should say a single short pilot is OK if the user explicitly asks, and should push agents to hand over a ready Euler command rather than only offering to write one.
Stats and junction-reset: both configurations passed everything. The plan doc and research notes already cover statistics and seed sets, so baseline agents read them.

Both junction-reset runs independently found a real E2 design bug: the alcove's back cue wall is visible straight down the corridor from the junction (edge ray of the 180° FOV), at every L. The coordinator confirmed it on rooms/twin_rooms_L*.json. A memoryless agent could re-read the cue, so E2 needs a geometry fix before launch.
Timing caveat: every run was interrupted by an API limit and resumed, so token/time figures may only cover the resumed part. Treat them as rough.
